newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche to detail 96 results Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche to detail 96 results Wednesday.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG, Germany's largest commercial bank, will on Wednesday release a full breakdown of its results for 1996, a year in which its image and earnings took a serious pounding.

The bank, which has already reported a 4.8 percent increase in net profit to 2.2 billion marks ($1.3 billion) and a stronger-than-expected 37 percent rise in operating earnings, is expected to reveal a substantial advance in own-account trading income for the year.

It may also give more details on the cost of the debacle at its Morgan Grenfell Asset Management unit in London, where the suspension of three funds amid allegations of mishandling led to compensation charges alone of around 200 million pounds ($323.3 million).
The bank is expected to have dissolved some of its hidden reserves to cope with the unexpected costs.

The full results will be released at a news conference from 0930 GMT, one day after an expected mass demonstration by steelworkers at Deutsche's Frankfurt headquarters -- a protest against Deutsche's role in supporting Krupp AG's now aborted hostile takeover bid for ribal Thyssen AG.
As well as its basic profit figures, Deutsche has also already said it plans an unchanged 1996 dividend of 1.80 marks.
Its balance sheet total jumped 23 percent to 886 billion marks due to increased trading activities as part of its expanding investment banking business.
Lending volume rose by 8.2 percent to 410 billion marks while customer deposits grew by 25 percent to 375 billion marks.
